criteria_results.title: IP section revised from ownership to perpetual-license construct
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 deletes the Customer-ownership language and instead provides that Vendor owns the Customer-Trained Adaptations while granting Customer an irrevocable, perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid-up license to use and modify the fine-tuned adapter weights and related artifacts.

criteria_results.title: Non-assertion covenant included in IP section
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 includes a broad Vendor non-assertion covenant in Section 5.2. Vendor irrevocably covenants, for itself and its successors and assigns, not to assert patent, copyright, trade secret, or other IP rights against Customer’s use, deployment, modification, or further development of exported Customer-Trained Adaptations, including use outside the Platform.

criteria_results.title: API-based weight export portability within 30 days in industry-standard format
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly requires API-based export of Customer-Trained Adaptations, including fine-tuned adapter weights, within 30 days after termination or expiration in an industry-standard format such as ONNX or SafeTensors.

criteria_results.title: Escrow provisions included as part of IP protective measures
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 includes a dedicated Technology Escrow framework in Article 5A and Exhibit E. It requires deposit and maintenance of fine-tuned adapter weights and Customer-Trained Adaptations, along with training configurations, scripts, pipeline artifacts, dependencies, and documentation needed to reproduce or redeploy them. These escrow protections are expressly linked to the perpetual-license construct in Sections 5.2 and 5A.3.

criteria_results.title: General liability cap at 1.5× annual fees ($3,600,000)
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 Section 10.2 sets the general aggregate liability cap at 1.5× the $2,400,000 Annual Platform Fee, expressly calculated as $3,600,000.

criteria_results.title: Super-cap at 3× annual fees ($7,200,000) for IP indemnity and data-breach carve-outs
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 10.3 applies a separate super-cap of three times the $2,400,000 Annual Platform Fee—$7,200,000—to both Vendor’s data-processing/data-breach liability under Article 6 and its IP indemnification obligations under Section 11.1.

criteria_results.title: Willful misconduct and gross negligence remain fully uncapped
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 10.3 expressly excludes liability arising from willful misconduct or gross negligence from the General Cap and states that such liability is uncapped. It also confirms that no provision may cap this liability, so the super-cap does not apply.

criteria_results.title: CCPA service-provider designation and certification
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly requires Vendor to act solely as a service provider/processor, states that Vendor is not an independent controller, and incorporates a DPA containing Vendor's certification that it is a “service provider” as defined in Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(ag).

criteria_results.title: Prohibition on use of Customer Data for model improvement with de-identification conditions
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly prohibits Vendor from using Customer Data, including de-identified or aggregated data, for model improvement, training, benchmarking, or product development unless the data satisfies the CCPA de-identification standard in Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(m) and the methodology is independently verified by a third-party assessor approved in writing by Customer (TechNova). This is stated as a specific contractual obligation in Section 6.9 and reinforced in the DPA.

criteria_results.title: Uptime SLA at 99.95% monthly
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 Section 9.1 requires Platform availability of at least 99.95% in each calendar month, and Exhibit B confirms the same monthly target.

criteria_results.title: Uptime SLA exclusions for scheduled maintenance and force majeure
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly excludes both scheduled maintenance windows and Force Majeure Events from uptime SLA downtime calculations in Section 9.1. Exhibit B also confirms these exclusions and specifies the conditions for scheduled maintenance.

criteria_results.title: Latency SLA at p95 ≤ 450 ms in Draft 3
criteria_results.reasoning: Although Section 9.2 and Exhibit B Section 4A use p95 ≤ 450 ms, Exhibit B’s service-level table inserts p95 ≤ 400 ms. Draft 3 therefore contains a conflicting latency SLA value rather than consistently setting it at 450 ms.

criteria_results.title: Issues list flags latency as yellow-zone item (450 ms vs. product team's 400 ms preference)
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list identifies the latency SLA as p95 ≤ 450 ms, expressly flags it as a yellow-zone caution, and notes that TechNova’s Product Engineering team prefers ≤ 400 ms.

criteria_results.title: F1 accuracy threshold at ≥ 0.92 initial
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 sets the initial model-accuracy threshold at F1 ≥ 0.92 during the Stabilization Period, including in Section 9.3, the Initial SOW, and Exhibit B. The former 0.90 threshold is shown as deleted text.

criteria_results.title: F1 ramp mechanism to ≥ 0.94 after 90-day stabilization period post-Go-Live
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 includes an express F1 ramp in Section 9.3 and the related SOW/SLA provisions: F1 ≥ 0.92 during the 90-day Stabilization Period following the October 1, 2025 Go-Live, increasing to F1 ≥ 0.94 beginning January 1, 2026 and thereafter.

criteria_results.title: SLA service credits capped at 20% of monthly fees ($40,000)
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly caps aggregate SLA Service Credits at 20% of the $200,000 monthly fee equivalent, equal to $40,000 per month, in Section 9.4 and Exhibit B.

criteria_results.title: Termination right for 3 consecutive months of SLA miss retained
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 retains Section 9.5, allowing Customer to terminate on 30 days’ notice if Vendor fails to meet any SLA target for three or more consecutive calendar months. The right is also repeated in Section 13.5 and Exhibit B.

criteria_results.title: New AI-output indemnity provision inserted
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 inserts a new Section 11.2, “AI-Output Indemnification,” requiring Vendor to defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer against third-party claims alleging that AI-generated Platform outputs, when generated and used within the documented use case, infringe third-party intellectual property rights or violate applicable law.

criteria_results.title: AI-output indemnity carve-out for Customer modification or off-label use
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 11.2 expressly excludes indemnity to the extent a claim is caused by Customer’s modification of an output after receipt or Customer’s use of the Platform or output outside the documented use case in the Agreement or SOW.

criteria_results.title: IP indemnity scope broadened to all intellectual property rights
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly broadens Section 11.1 to cover all Intellectual Property Rights worldwide—including patents, registered and unregistered copyrights, trademarks, trade secrets, know-how, moral rights, database rights, and analogous foreign rights—and applies the indemnity to Customer’s authorized use of the Platform, Base Model, outputs, and Customer-Trained Adaptations.

criteria_results.title: Escrow of adapter weights plus training configuration and pipeline artifacts
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 requires escrow of production fine-tuned adapter weights/Customer-Trained Adaptations, training configuration files, hyperparameters and training scripts, plus pipeline artifacts, orchestration/evaluation scripts, and workflow definitions. It expressly excludes the Base Model source code and Vendor’s general-purpose training infrastructure.

criteria_results.title: Iron Mountain IPM as proposed escrow agent with NCC Group as acceptable alternative
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 names Iron Mountain Intellectual Property Management, Inc. as the primary Escrow Agent in the agreement and Exhibit E. The updated issues list expressly identifies NCC Group plc as the acceptable fallback if it offers equivalent AI/ML escrow capability.

criteria_results.title: Escrow release triggers include insolvency, material uncured breach (>60 days), and cessation of product support
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 includes all three required escrow release triggers in Section 5A.3: Vendor insolvency/bankruptcy, a material breach remaining uncured for more than 60 days after notice, and cessation of support or maintenance (including announced discontinuation/end-of-life) of the Platform.

criteria_results.title: Tech E&O insurance accepted at $5M per occurrence in Draft 3
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 Section 12.1(b) sets Technology Errors & Omissions coverage at $5,000,000 per occurrence, expressly accepting Meridian’s current policy limit. The updated issues list also accurately reflects this treatment.

criteria_results.title: Issues list flags Tech E&O as yellow-zone item (playbook prefers $10M for TCV > $5M)
criteria_results.reasoning: Issue 11 flags the $5 million per-occurrence Tech E&O limit as a yellow-zone item and expressly states that the playbook prefers $10 million for TCV above $5 million, noting platform-fee TCV of $7.2 million.

criteria_results.title: Delaware governing law maintained in Draft 3
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 maintains Delaware governing law in Section 14.1, which states that the Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Delaware. No other state's law is specified as governing law.

criteria_results.title: Delaware courts (Court of Chancery or U.S. District Court for D. Del.) as dispute forum
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 14.2 requires disputes to be resolved in the Delaware Court of Chancery or the U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware, with Delaware Superior Court only as a fallback if Chancery declines jurisdiction. It does not require arbitration or use a Massachusetts forum.

criteria_results.title: DPA includes CCPA service-provider certification language
criteria_results.reasoning: Exhibit D expressly includes a “CCPA/CPRA Service-Provider Certification” stating that Vendor is a service provider as defined in Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(ag), will not sell or share Customer Data, and will not retain, use, or disclose it outside the direct business relationship or specified services and business purposes.

criteria_results.title: DPA includes GLBA safeguards compliance
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly addresses GLBA safeguards compliance. DPA Section 4 states that Customer Data includes consumer NPPI subject to GLBA and requires Vendor to comply with all applicable safeguard requirements. The main agreement also references the FTC Safeguards Rule in Section 6.3 and requires security controls in Section 6.4.

criteria_results.title: DPA includes 72-hour data breach notification
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3’s DPA, Section 8, requires Vendor to notify Customer of any confirmed or reasonably suspected Security Breach within seventy-two (72) hours after Vendor first becomes aware of or discovers it. This matches the required 72-hour timeline.

criteria_results.title: DPA includes sub-processor management with prior written consent
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3's DPA, Section 6 (Sub-Processor Requirements), expressly states that Vendor may not engage any sub-processor to process Customer Data without Customer's prior written consent. The main agreement's Section 6.6 likewise requires prior written consent for each engagement, appointment, or replacement.

criteria_results.title: DPA includes de-identification standards with statutory compliance and independent verification
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 satisfies both required elements. Section 6.9 and Exhibit D require de-identified data to comply with Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(m) and require the de-identification methodology to be independently verified by a third-party assessor approved in writing by Customer before use.

criteria_results.title: DPA includes data return/deletion upon termination
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 addresses data return/deletion upon termination in DPA Section 10, which requires Vendor to return or delete all Customer Data in accordance with Agreement Section 6.7 within 30 days of Customer’s written request and certify completion in writing.

criteria_results.title: Issues list covers all 12 minimum negotiation point categories
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list expressly covers all 12 required categories: IP ownership/licensing, liability cap, data processing/de-identification, uptime, latency, accuracy/F1, SLA credits, escrow, AI-output indemnity, IP indemnity scope, Tech E&O insurance, and governing law/dispute resolution.

criteria_results.title: IP ownership/licensing categorized as partially resolved
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes “IP ownership / license structure (perpetual license, portability, escrow, non-assertion)” as “Partially Resolved,” reflecting acceptance of the perpetual-license construct subject to unresolved protective conditions.

criteria_results.title: Liability cap categorized as partially resolved
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes the liability cap as “Open,” noting the proposed 1.5× ($3.6 million) compromise has not been accepted. The criterion expressly permits either “Partially Resolved” or “Open.”

criteria_results.title: Data processing/de-identification categorized as partially resolved
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes “Data processing / CCPA service-provider” as “Partially Resolved.” It states that service-provider classification and a DPA were agreed in principle, while the de-identification conditions were added in Draft 3 and remain TechNova’s proposed requirements rather than fully agreed terms.

criteria_results.title: Uptime SLA categorized as resolved
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes the 99.95% monthly uptime SLA as “Resolved” and notes the agreed scheduled-maintenance and force-majeure exclusions, including 72-hour maintenance notice.

criteria_results.title: Latency SLA categorized as partially resolved
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes latency as “Partially Resolved” and expressly states that 450 ms is accepted while the product team continues to prefer 400 ms.

criteria_results.title: Accuracy/F1 SLA categorized as open
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes “Accuracy / F1 score (0.92 ramp to 0.94)” as Open and states that Meridian has not agreed to the proposed ramp.

criteria_results.title: SLA credits categorized as partially resolved
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes SLA credits (Issue 4) as "Open," not fully "Resolved." This is expressly permitted by the criterion because the proposed 20% compromise has not been accepted by Meridian.

criteria_results.title: Escrow categorized as partially resolved
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes escrow as “Open,” reflecting that the concept may be agreed while scope and agent details remain disputed. The criterion expressly permits either “Partially Resolved” or “Open” and only fails a fully “Resolved” categorization.

criteria_results.title: AI-output indemnity categorized as open
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes issue 9, “AI-output indemnity,” as “Open,” consistent with Meridian not having substantively responded.

criteria_results.title: IP indemnity scope categorized as open
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes “IP indemnity scope (all IP rights / authorized use)” as “Open” and states that Meridian has not agreed to the broadened language.

criteria_results.title: Tech E&O insurance categorized as partially resolved with yellow-zone flag
criteria_results.reasoning: Issue 11, “Insurance / Tech E&O ($5 million accepted),” is categorized as “Partially Resolved” and expressly carries a “Yellow-zone caution” noting that $5 million is the Playbook minimum while $10 million is preferred.

criteria_results.title: Governing law/dispute resolution categorized as open
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes issue 12, “Governing law / dispute resolution,” as “Open” and expressly notes that it remains open with no movement.

criteria_results.title: Draft 3 is redlined against Draft 2 as the base (not Draft 1)
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 contains tracked insertions and deletions, and the companion issues list expressly states that it is a new redline against a clean base created by accepting all Draft 2 tracked changes. The document structure also reflects prior Draft 2 provisions as untracked base text while Draft 3 changes are tracked.

criteria_results.title: Annual platform fee preserved at $2,400,000/yr
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 preserves the Annual Platform Fee at $2,400,000 per Contract Year in Section 4.1, and the updated issues list confirms the same amount. The change to annual advance invoicing does not alter the annual fee.

criteria_results.title: 3-year initial term preserved (July 1, 2025 – June 30, 2028)
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 preserves the three-year Initial Term. The definition of “Initial Term” and Section 13.1 both state that it begins on July 1, 2025 and ends on June 30, 2028. The updated issues list confirms the same dates.

criteria_results.title: Implementation fee preserved at $850,000 with 50/50 milestone split
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 preserves the $850,000 implementation fee and splits it equally: $425,000 following execution of the Initial SOW (Milestone 1) and $425,000 following Go-Live (Milestone 2). The same terms are reflected in Exhibit A and the updated issues list.

criteria_results.title: Included API calls preserved at 40,000,000/yr with $0.012 overage
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 preserves 40,000,000 Included API Calls per Contract Year and an overage rate of $0.012 per API call in Section 4.3. The updated issues list also confirms the same terms.

criteria_results.title: 180-day auto-renewal notice period preserved
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 preserves the 180-day auto-renewal notice period. Section 13.2 requires either party to provide notice of non-renewal at least 180 days before the end of the then-current term, and the updated issues list confirms the same treatment.

criteria_results.title: Issues list notes latency 450 ms is within playbook acceptable range but below preferred 400 ms
criteria_results.reasoning: The issues list expressly states that p95 latency of 450 ms is acceptable under the Playbook’s ≤500 ms threshold but below the preferred ≤400 ms. It also ties the product team’s preference for sub-400 ms to LendStream’s synchronous consumer decisioning flow and calls for Product Engineering confirmation.

criteria_results.title: Issues list recommends considering latency escalation at the May 19 joint call
criteria_results.reasoning: The latency issue’s fallback/next-step entry expressly says to “revisit 400 ms or dedicated compute/regional deployment on the May 19 call,” and the call notes also list latency as a priority. This recommends addressing or considering escalation of latency at the planned joint call.

criteria_results.title: Issues list flags AI-output indemnity as fully open with no Meridian response
criteria_results.reasoning: The issues list marks AI-output indemnity as “Open,” but it does not state that Meridian has not substantively responded or that Delacroix acknowledged the issue on May 9 while indicating Meridian needed internal review.

criteria_results.title: Issues list notes playbook fallback for AI-output indemnity (shared-risk with vendor first-dollar coverage)
criteria_results.reasoning: The issues list expressly states under AI-output indemnity: “Fallback is a shared-risk framework with Vendor first-dollar coverage for defense, settlements, and judgments up to the applicable cap/super-cap.” This satisfies the required playbook fallback position.
